approach.method_basis: The Parent is a task-local molecular graph search with a population of the 64 best accepted molecules. It samples breeding parents from score-ranked quantiles, creates fresh offspring by connected-fragment crossover with optional finishing mutation or by one, two or three ordinary graph edits, and admits only stable canonical, unseen products that satisfy its size and source-relative sulfur rules. Before each announced batch it fits the inherited Gaussian process to every accepted molecule in that session, using chiral count-Morgan features and generalized Tanimoto covariance. It generates a fresh pool of 160 candidates and draws ten correlated posterior function rows. Position j buys the available maximum of row j, then removes that identity from later availability. After three consecutive batches without a strict improvement, only the forty highest posterior-mean candidates are initially eligible. The first improving batch resets the counter. The immediate Parent already removed a dormant rejection-conditioned mutation-length floor; its ordinary sampled edit lengths, crossover attenuation, GP, stalled screen and feedback loop remain present.
approach.novelty: This is the registered contribution control for the stalled eligibility screen on that exact Parent. It makes the full fresh pool eligible for the original ten Thompson choices while retaining the real stall counter and computing the original restricted choices passively on the same state and draws. The new result is a direct current-Parent contribution measurement, not a new optimizer. Same-Parent controls have removed residual influence within the restricted set; earlier screen removal used a winner-probability allocator, and recent gate changes used transformed predictive laws. Those tests leave different choices or different numerical models in place. This control changes only membership of the initial eligible set and keeps the original posterior and sampled maximum rule. The working prediction is that the retained screen helps this stack by preventing some lower-mean stalled purchases; the complete signed comparison can also show a harmful or negligible contribution without authorizing a new model-and-screen combination.

observed_bottleneck: The one behavior under test is the current Parent's exclusion of three quarters of a fresh pool during a real stall, despite unchanged correlated sampled function values being available for them. Read-only reconstruction from all fifteen n-cf8d309c06de Search logs and trajectories verifies 435 pools, 4350 optimizer purchases, 88 stalled announcements in 13 sessions, and zero posterior fallbacks. On those actual Parent states the original full-pool replay changes 77 ordered batches and 77 sets, substituting 215 identities; all 215 are outside the original top forty and no passive-only inside identity occurs on this particular panel. These passive choices have no newly observed scores. Complete Parent mean is 0.607030316211131, seed-macro population SD 0.030175277546149237; its three original summaries and run logs confirm 300 calls, 290 accepted optimizer proposals, zero invalids and zero duplicates per task. The source and current Candidate are byte-identical before APPLY. This measured exposure identifies a feasible control, not a prior contribution answer. The actual frozen catalog marks m-61b9b3bfb40d needs_evidence=true on this Parent. Historical n-61b9b3bfb40d adds the screen on an earlier Parent and records a +0.010577201922441012 endpoint contrast but unresolved component attribution; its original contribution target was the wider selector. The current Parent only deleted that ancestor's dormant mutation floor, so this is explicitly a narrowly scoped reverse control, not a newly discovered mechanism. n-0e978ade2613 removes the screen from fixed-field qPO, changes 75 paid outside-screen identities and loses 0.008737865918724682 against its own qPO Parent: positive retained contribution there, without transfer to sequential Thompson choices. n-ef26feaa2bbb changes the eligibility coordinate on a complete unit-linear warped host, has 14 actual-only purchases and a -0.0008284287153846881 endpoint contrast; it does not test screen presence. n-f45ac3b0bc90 also changes the gate coordinate on a different warped host and leaves ten essential predictive laws missing, so its +0.007594112734441327 endpoint contrast does not resolve contribution. The original reports and frozen catalog distinctions are preserved. Recounts and every source hash are in policy/scratch/r0071-03-improve-L01/evidence-audit.json and the fifteen audit-seed-N-task.json files; individual log/trajectory inputs accompany each audit. Source comparison is policy/scratch/r0071-03-improve-L01/source-audit.json.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse only the frozen review's internal bottleneck and applicability reasoning. Execute the single policy-authorized eligibility contribution control, keep the original model and proposal laws, and judge exact paid-choice exposure before its complete signed endpoint. Historical qPO and warped-gate results remain condition-specific. There are no paper adoptions, integration deviations, new models or dependencies.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: This control is based on the frozen current-Anchor contribution gap, actual original Thompson eligibility implementation, complete Parent Search exposure and competing eligibility explanations. The frozen Search Policy review was read, including its internal review and scope distinctions. Its external cardinal-learning and molecular-construction sources motivate other portfolio positions; none supplies a method element or efficacy claim used here. Therefore no external source or adoption is carried into this internal-evidence control, no new search is represented, and no introduced asset/dependency or method replacement requires one. Current-Parent source, fifteen original summaries/logs/trajectories and the original historical Analyze/source records are the evidence, with hashes in the local input manifest.

hypothesis: Validate m-61b9b3bfb40d on code Parent n-cf8d309c06de by removing only active consumption of its stalled top-mean eligibility restriction. Keep Evolution's exact K=3 non-improving-batch counter, announcement incumbent, strict-improvement reset and original M=40 request. At every successful FingerprintPosterior.select call compute the original ordered mask E_parent from (-original_mean,pool_index), restricted to min(40,pool_size) only when that real counter says stalled, but initialize active availability to every current fresh-pool index. For position j use the original already computed correlated sample row j, choose the first maximum in ascending original pool-index order among remaining active indices and remove only that chosen identity. Keep all ten original normal rows, mean, scale, covariance, Cholesky factor, jitters and numerical checks unchanged. Replay the original restricted sequence with a separate private availability mask over these same rows, only as evidence. This change should increase actual purchases that the original stalled screen excludes and thereby change subsequent accepted training and breeding inputs. The working prediction is positive retained mask contribution: with exact isolation, actual changed paid identities and complete matched outcomes, control-minus-Anchor delta is strictly below -0.002. The sign tests the total conditional control, including later adaptation, rather than asserting that outside-mask feedback alone mediates the endpoint.

finding_summary.headline: Opening the stalled pool admits 218 excluded purchases but lowers the endpoint, supporting the retained screen.
finding_summary.insights: The screen is doing more than withholding identities that would never reach learning: outside purchases changed predictions, survival and later breeding. Some were useful—eight beat their generating parents and one improved the incumbent—but their individual feedback cannot identify the cause of the total endpoint loss after adaptation. A useful distinction emerges: aggregate parent-beating offspring increased from 634 to 648 and positive generating-parent gain rose from 16.8912 to 17.2515, while final performance and late incumbent progress declined. More local wins were insufficient to improve the best result within this budget. Structural access also broadened: typed/generic scaffold counts rose from 1,668/952 to 1,740/1,016 and outside purchases were less similar to prior accepted molecules even after tiny fragments were excluded. Yet 25 of the 218 outside purchases were tiny fragments, and the Molecular assessment still finds late refinement of inherited families, uneven scaffold concentration and persistent reactive or strained motifs. This is not evidence of a universal scaffold collapse or a chemical cause of the score loss. A proposal method capable of useful core or linker changes while preserving favorable local functionality could address the observed limitation; this experiment cannot separate proposal quality from ranking quality or establish benefit from that method. The result settles the signed value of this screen on the tested stack and leaves its value after a different predictor or generator open.
finding_summary.results: All 435 allocations completed with the original sampling law. The control encountered 91 stalled pools and changed 75 purchase sets, admitting 218 molecules that the original screen would have excluded on those same states. All 211 eligible outside purchases entered the next model fit; 98 survived their batch and 37 later became breeding parents. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.607030 to 0.596453, a paired change of -0.010577. All three seed means fell; six of the fifteen task/seed endpoints improved, six declined and three tied. The largest losses were two sitagliptin endpoints. The exposed, isolated control therefore supports the predicted positive contribution of keeping the screen on this original Thompson stack. It does not meet the separate +0.002 performance-gain criterion.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heteroaromatic analogues with amines and carbonyls, but persistent reactive halogen bonds, strained closures and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: This is a descriptive reading of n-c501ea219a1c against its code Parent n-cf8d309c06de on the frozen Search seeds 0/1/2. context.comparison declares both complete Child evaluation and complete Parent pairing; all fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectories were present and read. Each panel contains 4,350 accepted optimizer molecules, excluding the ten initial observations per session from the census. Unpurchased pool molecules are not included. The Child ranges from 1 to 96 heavy atoms, with median 28; 4,239 molecules have rings and 4,213 have aromatic atoms. These graph readings agree with the digest ring-closure rates of 0.9598 to 0.9897 and aromatic-text rates of 0.9517 to 0.9782; the digest rates measure presence, not the fraction of atoms that are aromatic. The chemistry includes recognizable aryl carboxamides, fused azaheterocycles, cyclic amines, lactam-like carbonyls, ethers and thioethers. It also includes 786 molecules with N-halogen bonds, 217 with O-halogen bonds, 93 with S-halogen bonds, 127 with peroxide bonds, and 175 with a perceived ring of at most four atoms whose atoms are all aromatic. These overlapping flags are structural concerns, not measured instability or synthesis failures. Ordinary small rings are not intrinsically implausible. Sulfur occurs in 1,100 Child molecules versus 1,147 Parent molecules and spans thioethers, thiocarbonyls, sulfonyl-containing early products and unusual S-halogen groups; sulfur presence alone is not a liability. All Child and Parent molecules are written without formal charge or assigned tetrahedral stereochemistry. Potential unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 2,455 Child and 2,578 Parent molecules. Neutral SMILES does not mean a basic nitrogen cannot protonate. The Child has 105 molecules with at most five heavy atoms and 46 above fifty, compared with Parent 91 and 44. In the late half, optimizer ordinals 146 through 290 per session, the corresponding tails are 44 and 4 among 2,175 Child purchases, versus 33 and 3 for the Parent. Exact heavy-atom histograms, typed and generic Murcko counts, empty scaffolds, within-session concentrations, score ties and full/late strata are retained in the audit collection. The broad stream has many cores; some high-scoring families are concentrated, so a global collapse claim would be inaccurate. The Child observer receipts label 218 accepted purchases outside the original same-state screen, including 25 tiny fragments; 159 outside purchases are late. Using descriptive chiral 2048-bit radius-2 Morgan binary fingerprints, mean nearest-earlier-accepted similarity is 0.562130 outside and 0.719585 inside. Excluding queries and comparators with at most five heavy atoms gives 0.613143 outside and 0.730876 inside, on 193 and 4,052 molecules. Mean maximum similarity to actual generating parents is 0.533365 outside and 0.703976 inside, or 0.597519 and 0.717124 after the same fragment exclusion. Across all fragment-excluded purchases, nearest-history similarity is 0.725523 Child versus 0.731555 Parent, and generating-parent similarity is 0.711686 versus 0.717369. The Parent has no actual purchases outside its own screen, so that empty stratum has undefined similarities. These are associations on different adaptive histories, not evidence that structural novelty caused an endpoint change or that a mechanism activated. Synthetic plausibility is judged from connectivity only; no route, geometry, stability, pKa or additional objective was calculated. Reproducible derived evidence is indexed by policy/scratch/r0071-03-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json. Its fifteen immutable audit-seed-N-task.json files each record the task, frozen Search seed, exact trajectory and observer-log input paths, run-relative inputs and SHA256 hashes. Underlying Parent sources are the published files under nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2, individually cited in those audits. Underlying Child sources are the exact request-authorized .worktrees/slot-3/runs/staging trajectories and adjacent observer logs, individually recorded in the same audits. Those staging sources are outside runs/SPIRAL2 and the Child in-run archive does not yet exist; no future archive path is asserted to exist. Every cited_smiles below is an actual Child trajectory molecule. Parent-specific structures are compared descriptively. All transferable gaps retain this node, this Search panel and the accepted-stream scope; they are output limitations and hypotheses for a task-agnostic generator, not component attribution.

per_task.generated_character: Predominantly compact indole/azaindole-like fused aromatics attached to a phenyl or pyridyl group through a carbonyl-containing linker. Across 870 optimizer molecules, heavy atoms range 1-39 with median 24, and the median perceived ring count and aromatic-ring count are both 3. The upper examples carry N-hydroxy aryl carboxamides, alkyl/vinyl substituents and, often, halogen on the pyrrolic nitrogen. Seed 2 also explores adjacent thiocarbonyl/carbonyl or dicarbonyl linkers. There are 22 molecules with at most five heavy atoms and none above fifty. The Child has 250 typed/99 generic Murcko scaffolds, versus Parent 187/70, while the highest-scoring decile has only 16 typed/7 generic scaffolds. The recognizable aromatic/carboxamide framework is plausible as a medicinal-chemistry starting point; N-halogen and thiocarbonyl variants require much more chemical scrutiny.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 275 molecules, including 53 of the highest-scoring 87. N-hydroxyamides and thiocarbonyls also introduce redox, tautomeric or reactivity questions that were not measured.
Tiny fragments persist late, and peripheral halogen permutations can have identical observed scores; neither constitutional novelty nor aromaticity alone establishes useful chemistry.
missing_features: Upper records offer few independent core/linker arrangements combining the same compact size and aryl-carbonyl functionality; most remain close fused-heteroaromatic analogues. The trajectories do not establish one uniquely missing target motif.

Chemically conservative alternatives to N-halogen and thiocarbonyl substitutions are underrepresented among the leaders, although the high-scoring nonhalogenated N-hydroxyamide demonstrates that those liabilities are not indispensable to a high observed score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Cited molecule 1, seed 1 evaluation 293, scores 0.47411701813450596; it retains a three-ring aryl-carbonyl framework and adds an N-hydroxyamide while also carrying N-F. Molecule 2, seed 0 evaluation 281, reaches 0.4593573492521118 with an azaindole N-hydroxyanilide and no halogen. Molecule 3, a thiocarbonyl/carbonyl analogue, reaches 0.4369542269692598. The isolated halogen fragment in molecule 4 scores 0.0. Thus retained medium-sized heteroaryl/carbonyl architecture separates upper records from fragmentation; halogenation is not a necessary shared explanation. Molecules 5 and 6 both score exactly 0.4478476056206344 despite changes in halogen-bearing side groups, illustrating a local substituent plateau. Parent best values by seeds 0/1/2 are 0.42348216717712805, 0.4387992465191 and 0.45050436981567554, versus Child 0.4593573492521118, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.4369542269692598. Both panels stay largely within the same fused-aromatic/carbonyl chemistry; this comparison does not identify a target structure.

per_task.generated_character: A heterogeneous set of fused nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione systems, aryl ethers with C-N triple-bond groups, and nitroso-substituted aromatic amines. The 870 optimizer molecules have 1-96 heavy atoms, median 31, with median 4 perceived rings and 4 aromatic rings. There are 23 molecules with at most five heavy atoms and 20 above fifty. The largest product is an extensively concatenated nitrogen-rich polyaromatic structure, not a typical compact ligand. There are 343 typed/240 generic Murcko scaffolds, versus Parent 347/241, but only 13 typed/9 generic scaffolds in the upper decile. The upper seed-0 family contains a fused carbonyl/thione core, O-F and chlorinated ether substituents; seed 2 uses nitroso groups and short closures across an aromatic framework. These combinations make synthetic plausibility questionable even though many constituent aromatic and carbonyl groups are familiar.
liabilities: The stream includes 241 nitroso-containing molecules, 44 with O-halogen bonds and 79 with peroxide bonds. Of the highest-scoring 87, 49 carry nitroso groups and 21 have a perceived ring of at most four atoms with all atoms aromatic.

Hypofluorite, chlorinated ether, thione and compressed aromatic-ring motifs coexist in leading structures. These are reactivity or geometry concerns; no synthesis or geometry calculation establishes impossibility.
The high-size tail contains concatenated polyheteroaromatics up to 96 heavy atoms, while unrelated tiny fragments retain the same low plateau value.
missing_features: The high-scoring examples do not establish a comparably favorable set of conventional ring geometries and stable substituent combinations. Their scores cannot tell whether such more realistic alternatives would be rewarded.
There is no resolved stereochemical account of the newly saturated or bridged centres; the trajectory supports connectivity-level comparisons only, not a unique missing pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Cited molecules 1 and 2 both score 0.8561477222467935 while changing an N-substituent from a halogenated ether to a difluoromethyl group. Molecule 3, the nitroso-rich short-ring aromatic structure, scores 0.6442339647723496. Molecule 4, an isolated alkene, scores 0.5; this lower plateau also contains chemically unrelated fragments. The visible gradient favors retaining connected multiring heteroaromatic arrangements, but it also tolerates O-F, thione and unusually short ring closures. The 96-heavy-atom molecule 5 scores only 0.5628212450028556, so enlargement alone does not explain the upper examples. Parent and Child retain the same leading molecules and values in seeds 0 and 2; the seed-1 maxima are 0.6217289889933668 Parent and 0.6204376881838878 Child. The broad chemical character is therefore largely inherited rather than a new chemical class.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly halogenated diaryl structures bearing secondary/tertiary cyclic amines, with several aminal, bridged-amine and partially unsaturated small-ring families. The 870 optimizer molecules span 1-86 heavy atoms, median 29, and median 4 rings of which 2 are aromatic. The highest-scoring decile spans 24-33 heavy atoms; every member has two aromatic rings and an amine-like neutral nonaromatic nitrogen by the explicitly defined structural query. The leading seed-1 structure is a seven-membered diaza ring with an aminal centre, two aryl substituents, bromine, chlorine and a methylthio group. Seed 0 favors bridged cyclic amines and seed 2 aryl-substituted chromane-like systems with an unsaturated four-membered N ring. There are 18 molecules with at most five heavy atoms and 22 above fifty. Typed/generic scaffold counts are 370/232 versus Parent 327/202. The aryl-amine arrangement is familiar medicinal chemistry, but the aminal centre, compressed ring systems and absent configurations make the exact products less assured.
liabilities: Aminal centres occur in 257 molecules and 74 of the upper 87. Their substitution and likely speciation need chemical assessment beyond graph validity.

There are 254 products with a perceived three- or four-membered ring; the late seed-2 family combines an unsaturated four-membered N ring, multiple stereogenic centres and halogenated aromatic/alkyl groups.
A high-scoring S-F analogue and lower-scoring N/O-halogen products show that the visible objective does not itself certify stability or practical synthesis.
missing_features: Defined configurations are absent despite unassigned tetrahedral centres in all 87 upper-decile molecules. The favorable aryl/amine arrangement is present; its stereochemical alternatives have not been distinguished.

Explicit protonation states and lower-strain, non-aminal alternatives at a comparable aryl/amine arrangement are not demonstrated as a systematic set. The neutral representation still contains potentially basic centres, and the trajectory does not establish that charge enumeration would improve the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Cited molecule 1 scores 0.9999994532254913. Its S-F counterpart, molecule 2, scores 0.9999970978615854, so this close score is not evidence that the unusual S-F group is chemically acceptable. Molecule 3, a dichloroaryl sulfonamide/N-chloroamide product with no comparable free diaryl-amine arrangement, scores 0.00016650955053713697. All upper-decile molecules match the amine query and none carries sulfonyl, whereas 47 of the lowest-scoring 87 contain sulfonyl. The association is with the complete rearranged aryl/amine architecture, not a universal penalty on sulfur: the leading molecule itself has a thioether. The oversized molecule 5 has 86 heavy atoms and scores 0.028858525369541064. Parent and Child maxima by seed are respectively 0.980206046238846/0.9912539132815379, 0.9999921067161532/0.9999994532254913 and 0.9735180254338864/0.9817975835038065. Both panels remain diaryl-amine dominated; upper-decile sulfur-containing molecules increase from 6 to 31 without identifying sulfur as a causal contributor.

per_task.generated_character: Largely quinoline-like fused aromatic groups attached to nitrogen-rich medium-ring carbonyl systems, including N-methyl lactams, cyclic dicarbonyls, tertiary amines and some N-N-containing analogues. The 870 optimizer products span 1-68 heavy atoms, median 31, with median 4 perceived rings and 2 aromatic rings. There are 9 tiny fragments and 4 molecules above fifty heavy atoms. This task has substantial constitutional variety: 585 typed/392 generic Murcko scaffolds, including 56 typed/32 generic scaffolds in the highest-scoring 87. It is not a single-scaffold collapse. Relative to Parent, molecules with three/four-membered rings fall from 405 to 114 and aminal-containing molecules from 186 to 55, while the basic aromatic/dicarbonyl families persist. Many individual amide and amine groups are conventional, but their fused medium-ring arrangements and N-N/N-O variants need routes and stereochemical specification before being called straightforward synthesis targets.
liabilities: Medium-ring fusions, hydrazine-like N-N links and occasional N-O substitutions complicate conformational and synthetic interpretation, even when the local amide groups are conventional.
Potential unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 645 of the 870 products; no configurations are specified. The remaining small-ring and oversized products prevent a blanket plausibility claim.
missing_features: Configured alternatives for the substituted saturated and medium-ring centres are absent. Upper records preserve aromatic/dicarbonyl functionality but do not resolve its spatial presentation.

The many constitutional scaffolds do not identify a missing target-like motif or a chemically validated replacement family. A claim that the stream simply lacks rings, amides or basic nitrogen would contradict its own leaders.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Cited molecule 1, a propyl quinoline-like unit linked to a fused N-methyl dicarbonyl/amine ring system, scores 0.23233384457488657; the closely related shorter ring in molecule 2 scores 0.23092467462934307. The N-N-containing molecule 3 scores 0.2287776003289751. The isolated carbon molecule 4 scores 0.0, and the 68-heavy-atom concatenated molecule 5 scores 0.1202735457465673. All upper-decile molecules contain the defined amide motif, versus 33 of the lowest 87; retaining the combined fused aromatic and carbonyl-rich N-ring architecture is more consistent with the observed gradient than adding size or aromatic rings alone. Parent maxima by seed are 0.2228098910506594, 0.22127859918153825 and 0.24240057874100313; Child maxima are 0.2144511711621884, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.23233384457488657. The lower small-ring burden therefore does not by itself establish a better observed endpoint.

per_task.generated_character: Compact fluorinated nitrogen-rich oxo/imino heterocycles, often N-fluorinated, attached to a phenyl/cyclopentadienyl unit and a small partially saturated N ring or fluorinated side chain. The 870 optimizer molecules have 1-45 heavy atoms, median 27, with median 4 perceived rings and 3 aromatic rings. The leading seed-0 molecule is a ring-expanded conjugated N-rich oxo/imino system attached to a methoxy fluorocyclopentadiene and an unsaturated four-membered N ring; it should not be mistaken for an ordinary fully aromatic phenyl substituent. Seed 1 instead retains a phenolic aryl/oxo-heterocycle with fluoroalkyl substituents; seed 2 contains very short fused closures within an aromatic framework. There are 33 molecules with at most five heavy atoms and none above fifty, compared with Parent 17 and none. Typed/generic scaffold counts are 221/95 versus Parent 275/102; one Child session places 119 of 290 products on one typed scaffold. The mix of fluorination and nitrogen/carbonyl functionality is recognizable, but N-F/O-F bonds, diene rings and compressed closures make these exact products questionable synthesis targets.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 425 molecules, O-halogen in 82, and small three/four-membered rings in 281; these feature counts overlap and are not toxicity or stability measurements.

Seventy-five products contain a perceived ring of at most four atoms with all atoms aromatic, including the compressed seed-2 family. The leading seed-0 family also contains unsaturated four-membered N rings and cyclopentadienes.
The 33 tiny fragments, including monatomic fluorine and fluorine-fluorine species, score near the bottom and lack the connected functional-group arrangement seen in upper records.
missing_features: The upper examples do not supply a comparably rich set of chemically conventional alternatives retaining N-rich oxo/imino functionality and carbon-bound fluorination while avoiding N-halogen and short-ring motifs. Their unmeasured scores cannot be inferred.

Defined configurations are missing from stereogenic saturated substituents and ring junctions. None of the proposed structures specifies a tetrahedral configuration; 74 of the highest-scoring 87 have potential unassigned centres.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Cited molecule 1 scores 0.6942804632817005 and molecule 2, a fused-core analogue, 0.6658600050355483. Molecule 3 is the seed-2 leader at 0.6201223048692813, whereas elemental fluorine in molecule 4 scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. The upper decile stays between 24 and 29 heavy atoms and retains connected N-rich oxo/imino ring architecture with fluorinated substituents. N-halogen bonds remain in 65 of its 87 members, so the observed score does not require their removal. Molecule 5, carrying O-F on the heterocyclic nitrogen substituent, still scores 0.4868735382933089; the entire stream has 82 O-halogen products versus Parent 20. The Parent/Child maxima are 0.7658605860985803/0.6942804632817005, 0.6443701453126088/0.4999004646832901 and 0.6201223048692813/0.6201223048692813 by seed. These trajectories support a size/connectivity association but do not reveal an absent objective-specific answer structure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In n-c501ea219a1c on the frozen Search panel 0/1/2, the accepted optimizer stream has 786 N-halogen, 217 O-halogen, 93 S-halogen and 127 peroxide-containing molecules among 4,350; flags overlap. Published code-Parent n-cf8d309c06de has 888, 162, 107 and 118 under the same definitions. Some Child leaders retain these features, while another high-scoring N-hydroxyamide has no halogen. These are connectivity associations, not proven contributors or measured instability.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted chemistry does not consistently distinguish ordinary carbon halogenation from reactive heteroatom-halogen and peroxide chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need chemically contextual bond transformations and credible stable alternatives that preserve the surrounding scaffold and functional-group arrangement. Any stability-oriented construction should be tested against real session feedback rather than treating these flags as new objective rewards or asserting that every flagged bond is unusable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In n-c501ea219a1c on Search seeds 0/1/2, 175 of 4,350 accepted products have a perceived ring of at most four atoms with all atoms aromatic, and 903 have a three/four-membered ring; code-Parent n-cf8d309c06de has 170 and 1,172. The per-task witnesses include short closures through aromatic frameworks and unsaturated four-membered N rings. These are flags requiring geometry assessment, not a claim that all small rings are impossible.
transferable_gaps.gap: Constitutional ring variety is present, but geometric plausibility is not demonstrated for compressed aromatic closures and highly fused small rings.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring construction needs a way to preserve feasible aromatic connectivity and offer alternative ring sizes, fusion patterns and linkers without relying on compressed closures. Such output capability can be investigated without objective identity; it does not justify a blanket ban on useful small rings or promise an endpoint gain.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In n-c501ea219a1c on Search seeds 0/1/2, no accepted optimizer molecule has assigned tetrahedral stereochemistry, but 2,455 of 4,350 have an unassigned potential centre; the matched code-Parent n-cf8d309c06de has none assigned and 2,578 with unassigned centres. Both panels also use formally neutral SMILES, including molecules with potentially basic amines. The observed scores do not establish a stereochemical or protonation benefit.
transferable_gaps.gap: The stream supplies no assigned tetrahedral configurations even when it repeatedly builds potentially stereogenic centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to preserve and, where appropriate, enumerate configurations while making explicit which stereochemical identity is proposed. Protonation-state capability is a separate question: neutral representation must not be mistaken for absence of ionizable groups, and any additional identities need evaluation under the unchanged contract.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In n-c501ea219a1c on Search seeds 0/1/2, the accepted stream includes 105 molecules with at most five heavy atoms and 46 above fifty, versus code-Parent n-cf8d309c06de 91 and 44. Late Child purchases still contain 44 tiny fragments and 4 oversized products among 2,175. Of 218 receipt-labeled purchases outside the original same-state screen, 25 are tiny; removing these fragments raises mean nearest-history similarity from 0.562130 to 0.613143. The per-task witnesses show low-scoring elemental fragments and large concatenated structures, not uniformly useful novelty.
transferable_gaps.gap: Size-changing products do not reliably preserve a connected, informative functional-group arrangement at either size extreme.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic construction should be able to vary size while retaining meaningful attachment relationships and functional groups, and audit apparent novelty with both size tails explicit. These observations motivate better constructive edits or repair capability, not an unregistered size reward, universal minimum size or claim that all fragments are chemically worthless.

transferable_gaps.evidence: For n-c501ea219a1c on Search seeds 0/1/2, two upper-decile sets contain only 16 and 13 typed Murcko scaffolds among 87 products, whereas another contains 56; global collapse is therefore unsupported. A single session has 191 of 290 products on one generic scaffold, and another has 119 on one typed scaffold. Multiple halogen/substituent variants share exactly equal recorded scores. Fragment-excluded nearest-history similarity averages 0.725523 overall and 0.750219 late, compared with code-Parent n-cf8d309c06de 0.731555 and 0.755870.
transferable_gaps.gap: Fresh identities often remain peripheral variants of the same upper-scoring structural families, while broader constitutional variety is uneven across sessions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing output capability is a reliable supply of distinct core/linker arrangements that preserve favorable local functionality, alongside local analogues. Any task-agnostic proposal of that capability must distinguish scaffold counts from useful chemical alternatives and test feedback value; exact score ties and descriptive diversity do not identify a causal bottleneck by themselves.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
